schema_description: Living Hearing Profile — sovereign, user-owned, versioned hearing data. Extends openhear-audiogram-v1 with preference, context, haptic and history layers.
subject: Lewis Burgess

clinical_core.comment: Immutable clinical measurements. Append only via history layer; never mutate in place.
clinical_core.source: Dorothy Thomson Hearing Services, 12 Southend Ave, Darlington, DL3 7HL
clinical_core.notes: Most recent verified clinical audiogram. ISQ (no significant change) from prior tests dating back to 2017-01-19. High-frequency sloping sensorineural loss — the public reference profile for OpenHear.

preference_layer.comment: User-defined loudness and comfort preferences. Evolves over time as the user fine-tunes their experience. Refined with lived-experience signals through 2026-08-19.

loudness_growth.comment: Per-frequency gain offset applied on top of clinical prescription. Positive = louder, negative = quieter. Mid-frequency lift prioritised for speech intelligibility under high-frequency sloping loss.

preference_layer.notes: Stronger mid-band lift (1–2 kHz) after real-world confirmation that speech clarity in this region reduces listening fatigue for sloping losses. Sustained listening effort frequently leads to ‘switching off’. Lived-experience signal (2026-08-19, long-term aid user): amplified loudness itself can become the problem (recruitment / loudness intolerance) — people regularly remove aids or change programmes because the volume is overwhelming, even when residual environmental awareness remains. Preference layer and comfort ceiling must treat overload as a first-class failure mode, not only under-amplification. When an Auracast clean feed is active, preference offsets still apply; aggressive room-noise strategies should step down.

context_map.comment: Situational listening presets. Expanded through 2026-08-19 with lived-experience signals including multi-talker failure, background music, loudness overload leading to social avoidance, and medical appointment difficulty. See also docs/AURACAST.md and docs/HEARING_LOSS_AND_DEMENTIA.md.

contexts.name: quiet_conversation
contexts.label: Quiet room, one-to-one conversation
contexts.notes: Often the only setting where current aids feel helpful, especially face-to-face with lip-reading support.

contexts.name: familiar_speaker
contexts.label: Known / familiar talker (e.g. partner or regular voice)
contexts.notes: Lived-experience signal: familiar voices remain markedly easier than novel accents or unexpected conversational shifts. Supports lower processing aggression and reduced haptic load when the talker is known.

contexts.name: noisy_environment
contexts.label: Pub, restaurant, crowded social space
contexts.notes: Persistent failure mode even with modern premium aids. Residual environmental awareness can remain while speech intelligibility collapses. Multi-talker scenes, background music, and strong accents are common break points: the person hears that someone is speaking but misses key words or has no idea what was said. Loudness intolerance can make the aids themselves unbearable, leading to removal and, over time, avoidance of restaurants, parties, shops, and even some family gatherings. Primary target for effort reduction and complementary haptic support — not only more gain.

contexts.name: clinical_environment
contexts.label: Hospital ward / ICU / medical appointment — alarms + concurrent speech
contexts.notes: Alarms frequently mask concurrent speech. Medical appointments remain difficult when quiet areas are absent and professionals do not adjust for hearing needs; people often rely on family to interpret. Prefer selective haptic routing for alarms while preserving speech band.

contexts.name: phone_call
contexts.label: Telephone / video call
contexts.notes: Streaming can work for expected conversational strands; performance drops when the topic shifts, the speaker is unfamiliar, or more than one person speaks (group calls / Teams). Context-switch difficulty is cognitive as well as acoustic.

contexts.name: transport
contexts.label: Public transport — announcements and carriage noise

contexts.name: auracast_venue
contexts.label: Auracast / LE Audio broadcast — clean feed in a public space
contexts.notes: Bluetooth LE Audio Auracast delivers the original clean source (announcement, stage mic, TV channel, language track) rather than room acoustics. Prefer preference-layer shaping over aggressive room-noise strategies. Continuous stream speech should not drive continuous haptic voice pulses; haptic remains for discrete environmental events the broadcast does not cover, plus short join/leave cues. See docs/AURACAST.md.

haptic_layer.comment: Haptic substitution weights. Higher weight = stronger haptic signal for that sound category. Severity-weighted from the audiogram and refined with real-world priorities. Role of haptics includes a non-surgical bridge when speech-in-noise fails and when amplified loudness itself becomes intolerable. When an Auracast clean feed is active, continuous stream speech should not generate continuous voice haptics.

sound_classes.name: voice
sound_classes.note: Speech — highest priority in acoustic scenes. When an Auracast clean feed is carrying continuous speech, do not drive continuous haptic voice pulses; keep haptic for discrete events the broadcast does not replace. In overload / multi-talker scenes, short speech-onset cues can reduce the constant effort of catching the next word without adding more amplified noise.

sound_classes.name: alarm
sound_classes.note: Safety critical. Maximum haptic at the high-frequency band where this profile has the greatest loss. Route preferentially to haptic in clinical_environment context. Remains active even when an Auracast stream is joined.

sound_classes.name: infant_cry
sound_classes.note: High urgency for parent and clinical environments.

sound_classes.name: doorbell
sound_classes.note: High loss at 2 kHz drives strong substitution

sound_classes.name: traffic
sound_classes.note: Low-frequency traffic noise — kept lower priority than speech and safety sounds

sound_classes.name: media
sound_classes.note: General media — user can raise if desired

history.comment: Append-only change log with SHA-256 content commitments (Burgess Principle compatible). Each entry records what changed and a hash of the profile state at that point.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: First authentic non-placeholder commitment. Profile advanced from static 2021 clinical snapshot to a true Living Hearing Profile. Expanded context map with clinical/ICU and social-noise environments drawn from RNID Research Panel participant insights (12 Aug 2026). Strengthened mid-frequency preference offsets for speech under high-frequency sloping loss. Added infant_cry haptic class and raised priority of alarms and speech.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Incorporated further RNID-panel lived-experience signals: familiar voices vs novel accents; speech-in-noise failure despite residual environmental hearing; cusp-of-implant functional gap; sustained listening effort leading to switching-off.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Recorded complementary relationship with Bluetooth LE Audio Auracast. Added auracast_venue context. Continuous stream speech should not drive continuous voice haptics. See docs/AURACAST.md.

entries.author: Lewis Burgess
entries.description: Incorporated detailed RNID-panel lived experience (long-term aid user, multi-decade pathway): (1) recruitment / loudness intolerance — amplified sound becomes overwhelming and leads to aid removal even when residual environmental hearing remains; comfort ceiling treated as first-class failure mode; (2) multi-talker and background-music scenes where speech is present but not intelligible; (3) strong accents and group calls as repeated break points; (4) social and professional avoidance after overload, including some family gatherings and face-to-face work; (5) medical appointments remain difficult when quiet areas and professional adjustment are absent. Preference, noisy_environment, clinical_environment, and haptic notes strengthened accordingly. Parallel clinical-context note added: docs/HEARING_LOSS_AND_DEMENTIA.md (association vs causation; OpenHear justified by lived function, not dementia-prevention claims).
